#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Write the test data, deterministic from a seed number.

    python3 gen_fixture.py --seed 7 --out fixture          seed.jsonl, ops.jsonl, planted.json
    python3 gen_fixture.py --small --out fixture_small     the six-node graph and ops_a/b/c.jsonl

Every id and every choice comes from one random generator started with the seed, so the same seed always
gives the same files. Before writing, the generator counts what the task asks for, prints the counts, and
stops with an error if one is missed.

The main fixture: a data catalog (two databases, eight schemas, ~110 tables, ~1,400 columns, 150
dashboards). The first operation deletes the warehouse.sales schema (500+ nodes). Then about 300 mixed
operations: people editing the neighbours of the deleted area, an ingest run that recreates 50+ of the
deleted names under new ids, people editing those recreated nodes, arrows re-pointed, and arrows added.
Random data alone might never reach a rare rule, so the generator also plants one case for each rule and
lists them in planted.json, which the checker reads.

Each operation is applied to the replay (replay.py) as it is written, so later choices see its effect, and
the generator stops if an operation it meant to be valid is rejected.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import random
import sys
import uuid
from collections import defaultdict
from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from replay import Replay, ingest_node_id

PEOPLE = ["asha", "ben", "dana", "eli", "farah", "gus", "hana", "ivan", "jo", "kai", "lena", "mo", "noor", "omar"]
# gdpr is kept out of the seed: a person adds it above the deleted root, and restored nodes must pick it up.
TAGS = ["finance", "pii", "contact", "internal", "public", "sensitive", "raw", "curated", "daily", "certified"]
TABLE_WORDS = [
    "orders", "refunds", "customers", "invoices", "payments", "shipments", "returns", "discounts",
    "carts", "sessions", "leads", "accounts", "contracts", "quotes", "subscriptions", "renewals",
    "regions", "territories", "targets", "commissions", "products", "prices", "promotions", "channels",
    "partners", "events", "tickets", "campaigns", "budgets", "employees", "payroll", "vendors",
    "assets", "ledgers", "forecasts", "inventory", "stores", "suppliers", "audits", "surveys",
]
COLUMN_WORDS = [
    "id", "created_at", "updated_at", "amount", "currency_code", "email", "phone", "full_name",
    "status", "region", "country", "city", "postal_code", "customer_id", "order_id", "product_id",
    "quantity", "unit_price", "discount", "tax", "total", "notes", "source", "channel",
    "segment", "score", "owner_id", "due_date", "paid_at", "method", "card_last4", "ip_address",
    "user_agent", "referrer", "campaign_id", "margin", "cost", "weight", "sku", "category",
]
PII_COLUMNS = {"email", "phone", "full_name", "postal_code", "card_last4", "ip_address", "user_agent"}
DASHBOARD_WORDS = ["revenue", "growth", "churn", "pipeline", "funnel", "margin", "retention", "ops", "health"]
# (database, schema, number of tables, (min, max) columns per table)
LAYOUT = [
    ("warehouse", "sales", 26, (19, 26)),
    ("warehouse", "marketing", 13, (8, 14)),
    ("warehouse", "finance", 13, (8, 14)),
    ("warehouse", "hr", 12, (8, 14)),
    ("warehouse", "ops", 12, (8, 14)),
    ("warehouse", "product", 12, (8, 14)),
    ("lake", "raw", 10, (6, 12)),
    ("lake", "staging", 10, (6, 12)),
]
DASHBOARDS = 150
DELETED_SCHEMA = "warehouse.sales"
OPS_AFTER_DELETE = 300


# ---- seed -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def build_seed(rng: random.Random) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    nodes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    contains: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    refs: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()

    def new_id() -> str:
        return str(uuid.UUID(int=rng.getrandbits(128), version=4))

    def person(p: float) -> str | None:
        return rng.choice(PEOPLE) if rng.random() < p else None

    def some_tags(most: int) -> list[str]:
        return rng.sample(TAGS, rng.randint(0, most))

    def add_node(node_id: str, name: str, node_type: str, description: str | None, owner: str | None, tags: list[str]) -> str:
        nodes.append(
            {
                "kind": "node",
                "id": node_id,
                "qualified_name": name,
                "type": node_type,
                "description": description,
                "owner": owner,
                "tags": tags,
            }
        )
        return node_id

    databases = {
        "warehouse": add_node(new_id(), "warehouse", "database", "Central warehouse", "asha", ["internal"]),
        "lake": add_node(new_id(), "lake", "database", "Raw landing zone", "omar", ["raw"]),
    }
    tables: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    columns: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for db_name, schema, n_tables, (cmin, cmax) in LAYOUT:
        schema_name = f"{db_name}.{schema}"
        schema_id = add_node(new_id(), schema_name, "schema", f"{schema.capitalize()} schema", person(0.7), some_tags(1))
        contains.append((databases[db_name], schema_id))
        tables[schema_name] = []
        for word in sorted(rng.sample(TABLE_WORDS, n_tables)):
            table_name = f"{schema_name}.{word}"
            table_id = add_node(
                new_id(), table_name, "table", f"{word.capitalize()} in {schema}", person(0.85), some_tags(2)
            )
            contains.append((schema_id, table_id))
            tables[schema_name].append(table_id)
            columns[table_id] = []
            for col in sorted(rng.sample(COLUMN_WORDS, rng.randint(cmin, cmax))):
                tags = ["pii"] if col in PII_COLUMNS else []
                tags += [t for t in some_tags(1) if t not in tags]
                description = f"{col.replace('_', ' ').capitalize()} of {word}" if rng.random() < 0.9 else None
                column_id = add_node(new_id(), f"{table_name}.{col}", "column", description, person(0.4), tags)
                contains.append((table_id, column_id))
                columns[table_id].append(column_id)

    reports = add_node(new_id(), "reports", "folder", "Dashboards", None, ["public"])
    sales_tables = tables[DELETED_SCHEMA]
    other_tables = [t for name, ts in tables.items() if name != DELETED_SCHEMA for t in ts]
    for i in range(DASHBOARDS):
        word = rng.choice(DASHBOARD_WORDS)
        dashboard = add_node(
            new_id(), f"reports.{word}_{i:03d}", "dashboard", f"{word.capitalize()} dashboard {i}", person(0.7),
            some_tags(1),
        )
        contains.append((reports, dashboard))
        targets: set[str] = set()
        want = rng.randint(5, 11)
        while len(targets) < want:
            table = rng.choice(sales_tables if rng.random() < 0.3 else other_tables)
            targets.add(rng.choice(columns[table]) if rng.random() < 0.35 else table)
        refs.update((dashboard, target) for target in targets)
    all_tables = sales_tables + other_tables
    for table in all_tables:  # lineage: a table is built from other tables
        for _ in range(rng.choice((0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 3))):
            source = rng.choice(all_tables)
            if source != table:
                refs.add((table, source))
    return (
        nodes
        + [{"kind": "edge", "from_id": p, "to_id": c, "type": "contains"} for p, c in sorted(contains)]
        + [{"kind": "edge", "from_id": f, "to_id": t, "type": "references"} for f, t in sorted(refs)]
    )


# ---- operations -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class Ops:
    """Writes operations, applying each one to the replay so the next one sees its effect."""

    def __init__(self, replay: Replay) -> None:
        self.r = replay
        self.lines: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self.human_edits: list[str] = []  # node ids a person edited, in order
        self.repointed = 0
        self.expected_rejections = 0
        self.ingest_created: dict[str, str] = {}  # name -> id, for every node an ingest created

    def _apply(self, actor: str, kind: str, *, rejected: bool = False, **fields: Any) -> str:
        op_id = f"op{len(self.lines) + 1:04d}"
        op = {"op_id": op_id, "actor": actor, "kind": kind, **fields}
        self.lines.append(op)
        reason = self.r.apply(len(self.lines), op)
        if rejected != (reason is not None):
            raise SystemExit(f"gen_fixture: {op_id} should {'not ' * (not rejected)}be rejected ({reason}): {op}")
        return op_id

    def delete(self, root: str) -> str:
        return self._apply("human", "delete_subtree", root_id=root)

    def edit(self, node_id: str, **changes: Any) -> None:
        self._apply("human", "edit_node", id=node_id, set=changes)
        self.human_edits.append(node_id)

    def ingest(self, name: str, node_type: str, parent_name: str | None) -> str:
        created = name not in self.r.by_name
        self._apply("ingest", "ingest_node", qualified_name=name, type=node_type, parent=parent_name)
        if created:
            self.ingest_created[name] = self.r.by_name[name]
        return self.r.by_name[name]

    def add_ref(self, actor: str, from_id: str, to_id: str) -> None:
        self._apply(actor, "add_edge", from_id=from_id, to_id=to_id, type="references")

    def repoint_ref(self, from_id: str, to_id: str, new_to: str) -> None:
        self._apply("human", "repoint_edge", from_id=from_id, to_id=to_id, type="references", new_to_id=new_to)
        self.repointed += 1

    def move(self, child: str, new_parent: str) -> None:
        self._apply(
            "human", "repoint_edge", from_id=self.r.parent[child], to_id=child, type="contains", new_from_id=new_parent
        )
        self.repointed += 1

    def rejected(self, actor: str, kind: str, **fields: Any) -> None:
        """An operation the tool must refuse; nothing changes."""
        self._apply(actor, kind, rejected=True, **fields)
        self.expected_rejections += 1


def build_ops(r: Replay, rng: random.Random) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
    w = Ops(r)
    warehouse = r.by_name["warehouse"]
    sales = r.by_name[DELETED_SCHEMA]
    siblings = [c for c in r.children_of(warehouse) if c != sales]
    doomed = set(r.subtree(sales))
    old = {node_id: dict(r.nodes[node_id]) for node_id in doomed}
    referrers = sorted({f for f, t in r.refs if t in doomed and f not in doomed})
    dashboards = {n for n, v in r.nodes.items() if v["type"] == "dashboard"}
    sales_tables = r.children_of(sales)
    columns_of = {t: r.children_of(t) for t in sales_tables}
    table_referrers = {t: sorted(d for d in dashboards if (d, t) in r.refs) for t in sales_tables}
    live_refs_after = defaultdict(set)  # dashboard -> targets that survive the delete
    for f, t in r.refs:
        if f in dashboards and t not in doomed:
            live_refs_after[f].add(t)

    # ---- 1. the delete --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    delete_op = w.delete(sales)

    # ---- roles for the planted cases --------------------------------------------------------------
    tables = sales_tables[:]
    rng.shuffle(tables)

    def take(pred: Callable[[str], bool]) -> str:
        for t in tables:
            if pred(t):
                tables.remove(t)
                return t
        raise SystemExit("gen_fixture: no table fits a planted case; try another seed")

    t_g = take(lambda t: any(live_refs_after[d] for d in table_referrers[t]))
    d_g = next(d for d in table_referrers[t_g] if live_refs_after[d])
    t_h = take(lambda t: any(d != d_g for d in table_referrers[t]))
    d_h = next(d for d in table_referrers[t_h] if d != d_g)
    t_a = take(lambda t: bool(old[t]["description"] and old[t]["owner"] and old[t]["tags"]))
    t_b = take(lambda t: old[t]["owner"] not in (None, "ben"))
    t_c = take(lambda t: old[t]["owner"] is not None)
    t_d = take(lambda t: True)
    t_view = take(lambda t: True)
    t_e = take(lambda t: True)
    t_f = take(lambda t: True)
    t_x = take(lambda t: True)
    extra_recreated = [tables.pop() for _ in range(5)]
    recreated_tables = [t_a, t_b, t_c, t_d, t_view, t_e, t_g, t_h] + extra_recreated
    protected = {d_g, d_h}  # random operations never touch these, so the planted cases stay as planted

    def name(node_id: str) -> str:
        return old[node_id]["qualified_name"]

    # ---- 2. people work next to the deleted area (independent edits) ----------------------------
    w.edit(warehouse, tags=r.nodes[warehouse]["tags"] + ["gdpr"])  # a tag added above the deleted root
    w.edit(warehouse, description="Central warehouse, EU region")
    for sibling in siblings:
        w.edit(sibling, owner=rng.choice(PEOPLE))
    for referrer in rng.sample([x for x in referrers if x not in protected], 10):
        w.edit(referrer, description=f"{r.nodes[referrer]['description'] or 'Reworked'} (reworked after cleanup)")

    # ---- 3. the ingest run ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    new: dict[str, str] = {}  # old id -> id of the node the ingest created under the same name
    new[sales] = w.ingest(DELETED_SCHEMA, "schema", "warehouse")
    order = recreated_tables[:]
    rng.shuffle(order)
    e_col = None
    for t in order:
        new[t] = w.ingest(name(t), "view" if t == t_view else "table", DELETED_SCHEMA)
        cols = columns_of[t]
        picked = sorted(rng.sample(cols, rng.randint(3, 5)))
        for c in picked:
            new[c] = w.ingest(name(c), "column", name(t))
        if t == t_e:
            e_col = next(c for c in cols if c not in picked)  # stays deleted, its parent comes back
    f_col = columns_of[t_f][0]  # recreated while its table is not: lands at the top level
    new[f_col] = w.ingest(name(f_col), "column", name(t_f))
    x_col = columns_of[t_x][0]  # parent and child swapped by the ingest source
    new[x_col] = w.ingest(name(x_col), "column", name(t_x))
    new[t_x] = w.ingest(name(t_x), "table", name(x_col))
    for t in rng.sample([t for t in recreated_tables if t != t_a], 3):  # a column that never existed
        w.ingest(f"{name(t)}.currency", "column", name(t))
    for t in recreated_tables:  # ingest re-adds a dashboard's arrow to the recreated table
        if t in (t_g, t_h):
            continue
        for d in table_referrers[t]:
            if d not in protected and (d, new[t]) not in r.refs:
                w.add_ref("ingest", d, new[t])
                break
    w.add_ref("ingest", d_h, new[t_h])
    live_other_tables = sorted(
        n for n, v in r.nodes.items()
        if v["type"] == "table" and n not in new.values() and r.parent.get(n) in siblings
    )
    for i, t in enumerate(rng.sample(live_other_tables, 10)):  # ingest re-reports live tables
        w.ingest(r.nodes[t]["qualified_name"], "view" if i == 0 else "table", r.nodes[r.parent[t]]["qualified_name"])

    # ---- 4. people work on the recreated nodes and around them ----------------------------------
    recreated_cols = sorted(new[c] for c in new if c in old and old[c]["type"] == "column" and c not in (f_col, x_col))
    hashed_col, described_col = rng.sample([c for c in recreated_cols if r.parent.get(c) != new[t_a]], 2)
    sibling_for_d = rng.choice(siblings)
    planted: list[Callable[[], None]] = [
        lambda: w.edit(new[t_b], owner="ben"),
        lambda: w.edit(new[t_c], owner=None),  # emptied on purpose: the ingest left it empty, a person says so
        lambda: w.edit(hashed_col, description="Hashed before load", tags=["hashed"], owner=None),
        lambda: w.edit(described_col, description="Rebuilt by ingest, checked by hand"),
        lambda: w.edit(new[sales], owner="farah"),
        lambda: w.move(new[t_d], sibling_for_d),
        lambda: w.repoint_ref(d_g, sorted(live_refs_after[d_g] & {t for f, t in r.refs if f == d_g})[0], new[t_g]),
        lambda: w.repoint_ref(d_h, new[t_h], _free_target(r, rng, d_h, protected | set(new.values()))),
    ]
    # Random edits leave the planted nodes alone: the untouched node stays untouched, the owner a person set
    # (or emptied) stays as planted, and the tag added above the root is never taken off again.
    no_random_edit = {warehouse, new[t_a], new[t_b], new[t_c]}
    edit_pools = {
        "neighbour": [n for n in siblings + referrers if n not in protected],
        "recreated": [n for n in new.values() if n not in no_random_edit],
    }

    def random_edit() -> None:
        roll = rng.random()
        if roll < 0.35:
            pool = edit_pools["neighbour"]
        elif roll < 0.5:
            pool = edit_pools["recreated"]
        else:
            pool = list(r.nodes)
        node_id = rng.choice(sorted(n for n in pool if n in r.nodes and n not in no_random_edit))
        node = r.nodes[node_id]
        kind = rng.choice(("description", "owner", "tags", "both"))
        changes: dict[str, Any] = {}
        if kind in ("description", "both"):
            changes["description"] = f"{node['qualified_name']} — note {len(w.lines)}"
        if kind in ("owner", "both"):
            changes["owner"] = rng.choice(PEOPLE) if rng.random() < 0.9 else None
        if kind == "tags":
            tags = list(node["tags"])
            if tags and rng.random() < 0.4:
                tags.remove(rng.choice(tags))
            else:
                extra = rng.choice([t for t in TAGS if t not in tags] or TAGS)
                if extra not in tags:
                    tags.append(extra)
            changes["tags"] = tags
        w.edit(node_id, **changes)

    def random_repoint() -> None:
        candidates = sorted((f, t) for f, t in r.refs if f in dashboards and f not in protected and t not in protected)
        from_id, to_id = rng.choice(candidates)
        w.repoint_ref(from_id, to_id, _free_target(r, rng, from_id, protected))

    def random_add() -> None:
        from_id = rng.choice(sorted(d for d in dashboards if d in r.nodes and d not in protected))
        w.add_ref("human", from_id, _free_target(r, rng, from_id, protected))

    def random_move() -> None:
        movable = sorted(
            t for t in r.nodes
            if r.nodes[t]["type"] == "table" and r.parent.get(t) in siblings and t not in new.values()
        )
        child = rng.choice(movable)
        w.move(child, rng.choice([s for s in siblings if s != r.parent[child]]))

    rejections: list[Callable[[], None]] = [
        lambda: w.rejected("human", "edit_node", id=t_a, set={"owner": "zed"}),  # old id, not live
        lambda: w.rejected(  # warehouse under one of its own tables: a loop
            "human", "add_edge", from_id=rng.choice(r.children_of(siblings[0])), to_id=warehouse, type="contains"
        ),
        lambda: w.rejected(  # an arrow that is not there
            "human", "repoint_edge", from_id=d_g, to_id=t_g, type="references", new_to_id=warehouse
        ),
    ]
    late_ingest = [new[t] for t in recreated_tables[:6]] + [new[t_view]]
    fixed = len(planted) + len(rejections) + len(late_ingest)
    n_random = OPS_AFTER_DELETE - (len(w.lines) - 1) - fixed
    weights = [(random_edit, 0.62), (random_repoint, 0.18), (random_add, 0.12), (random_move, 0.08)]
    actions: list[Callable[[], None]] = planted + rejections
    for _ in range(n_random):
        roll, acc = rng.random(), 0.0
        for fn, weight in weights:
            acc += weight
            if roll < acc:
                actions.append(fn)
                break
        else:
            actions.append(random_edit)
    rng.shuffle(actions)
    for action in actions:
        action()

    # ---- 5. a late ingest pass re-reports some recreated tables -------------------------------------
    for node_id in late_ingest:
        parent = r.parent.get(node_id)
        w.ingest(r.nodes[node_id]["qualified_name"], r.nodes[node_id]["type"], r.nodes[parent]["qualified_name"] if parent else None)

    # ---- counts the task asks for ------------------------------------------------------------------
    deleted_names = {v["qualified_name"] for v in old.values()}
    recreated_names = sorted(n for n in w.ingest_created if n in deleted_names)
    recreated_ids = {w.ingest_created[n] for n in recreated_names}
    human_after = set(w.human_edits)
    counts = {
        "delete_op": delete_op,
        "deleted_nodes": len(r.deletes[delete_op]["nodes"]),
        "operations_after_delete": len(w.lines) - 1,
        "human_edits_to_parent": w.human_edits.count(warehouse),
        "human_edits_to_siblings": sum(w.human_edits.count(s) for s in siblings),
        "human_edits_to_referrers": sum(1 for n in w.human_edits if n in set(referrers)),
        "edges_repointed": w.repointed,
        "deleted_names_recreated_by_ingest": len(recreated_names),
        "recreated_nodes_edited_by_people": len(recreated_ids & human_after),
        "expected_rejections": w.expected_rejections,
    }
    minimums = {
        "delete removes at least 500 nodes": counts["deleted_nodes"] >= 500,
        "about 300 operations after the delete": 250 <= counts["operations_after_delete"] <= 350,
        "people edit the parent of the deleted area": counts["human_edits_to_parent"] >= 1,
        "people edit siblings of the deleted area": counts["human_edits_to_siblings"] >= 1,
        "people edit nodes that referenced the deleted area": counts["human_edits_to_referrers"] >= 1,
        "edges are re-pointed to other nodes": counts["edges_repointed"] >= 1,
        "ingest recreates at least 50 deleted names under new ids": counts["deleted_names_recreated_by_ingest"] >= 50,
        "people edit at least 5 recreated nodes": counts["recreated_nodes_edited_by_people"] >= 5,
        "nobody edits the untouched recreated node": new[t_a] not in human_after,
    }
    planted_cases = {
        "delete_op": delete_op,
        "cases": {
            "untouched_recreated": {"old_id": t_a, "new_id": new[t_a]},
            "person_changed_field": {"old_id": t_b, "new_id": new[t_b], "field": "owner", "value": "ben"},
            "person_emptied_field": {"old_id": t_c, "new_id": new[t_c], "field": "owner"},
            "recreated_moved": {"old_id": t_d, "new_id": new[t_d], "old_parent": sales, "new_parent": sibling_for_d},
            "restored_under_recreated_parent": {"id": e_col, "parent_old": t_e, "parent_new": new[t_e]},
            "recreated_child_of_free_parent": {"parent_id": t_f, "old_id": f_col, "new_id": new[f_col]},
            "repointed_onto_recreated": {"from": d_g, "old_to": t_g, "new_to": new[t_g]},
            "repointed_away": {"from": d_h, "old_to": t_h, "new_to": new[t_h]},
            "type_differs": {"old_id": t_view, "new_id": new[t_view], "old_type": "table", "new_type": "view"},
            "tag_above_root": {"node": warehouse, "tag": "gdpr", "restored_id": e_col},
            "swapped_parent_child": {
                "schema_old": sales,
                "table_old": t_x,
                "table_new": new[t_x],
                "column_old": x_col,
                "column_new": new[x_col],
            },
        },
    }
    return w.lines, counts, {"minimums": minimums, "planted": planted_cases}


def _free_target(r: Replay, rng: random.Random, from_id: str, avoid: set[str]) -> str:
    """A live table or column that from_id does not reference yet."""
    taken = {t for f, t in r.refs if f == from_id}
    pool = sorted(
        n for n, v in r.nodes.items()
        if v["type"] in ("table", "column") and n not in taken and n not in avoid and n != from_id
    )
    return rng.choice(pool)


def build_main(seed: int) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any], dict[str, bool]]:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    seed_lines = build_seed(rng)
    ops, counts, extra = build_ops(Replay(seed_lines), rng)
    counts = {
        "seed_nodes": sum(1 for line in seed_lines if line["kind"] == "node"),
        "seed_edges": sum(1 for line in seed_lines if line["kind"] == "edge"),
        **counts,
    }
    files = {"seed.jsonl": seed_lines, "ops.jsonl": ops, "planted.json": extra["planted"]}
    return files, counts, extra["minimums"]


# ---- the small fixture --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def small_id(short: str) -> str:
    return f"00000000-0000-4000-8000-{int(short[1:]):012d}"


def build_small() -> dict[str, Any]:
    nodes = [
        ("n1", "sales", "schema", "Sales schema", None, ["finance"]),
        ("n2", "sales.orders", "table", "One row per order", "asha", ["pii"]),
        ("n5", "sales.refunds", "table", "One row per refund", None, []),
        ("n3", "sales.orders.email", "column", "Customer email", "dana", ["contact"]),
        ("n4", "sales.orders.total", "column", "Order total, EUR", "asha", []),
        ("n6", "reports.daily", "dashboard", "Daily revenue", None, []),
    ]
    edges = [
        ("n1", "n2", "contains"),
        ("n1", "n5", "contains"),
        ("n2", "n3", "contains"),
        ("n2", "n4", "contains"),
        ("n6", "n2", "references"),
        ("n6", "n4", "references"),
    ]
    seed = [
        {"kind": "node", "id": small_id(s), "qualified_name": q, "type": t, "description": d, "owner": o, "tags": g}
        for s, q, t, d, o, g in nodes
    ] + [{"kind": "edge", "from_id": small_id(a), "to_id": small_id(b), "type": t} for a, b, t in edges]

    def delete(op_id: str, root_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"op_id": op_id, "actor": "human", "kind": "delete_subtree", "root_id": root_id}

    recreated = ingest_node_id("i1", "sales.orders")
    return {
        "seed.jsonl": seed,
        # A neighbour is deleted later: d2 removes the dashboard that two arrows of d1 need.
        "ops_a.jsonl": [delete("d1", small_id("n2")), delete("d2", small_id("n6"))],
        # The parent is deleted later: d2 removes sales, the parent of the subtree d1 removed.
        "ops_b.jsonl": [delete("d1", small_id("n2")), delete("d2", small_id("n1"))],
        # The recreated node is deleted again: two old versions of sales.orders end up in two journals.
        "ops_c.jsonl": [
            delete("d1", small_id("n2")),
            {"op_id": "i1", "actor": "ingest", "kind": "ingest_node", "qualified_name": "sales.orders",
             "type": "view", "parent": "sales"},
            {"op_id": "e1", "actor": "human", "kind": "edit_node", "id": recreated, "set": {"owner": "ben"}},
            delete("d2", recreated),
        ],
    }


# ---- writing ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _render(name: str, content: Any) -> str:
    if name.endswith(".jsonl"):
        return "".join(json.dumps(line, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n" for line in content)
    return json.dumps(content, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"


async def _write_all(out: Path, files: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    await asyncio.to_thread(out.mkdir, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    await asyncio.gather(
        *(asyncio.to_thread((out / name).write_text, _render(name, content), "utf-8") for name, content in files.items())
    )


async def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=7, help="random seed (default 7)")
    parser.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="directory to write into")
    parser.add_argument("--small", action="store_true", help="write the six-node fixture instead")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    out = Path(args.out)

    if args.small:
        files = build_small()
        await _write_all(out, files)
        print(json.dumps({"wrote": sorted(files)}, indent=2))
        return 0

    files, counts, minimums = await asyncio.to_thread(build_main, args.seed)
    print(json.dumps({"seed": args.seed, **counts}, indent=2))
    for rule, ok in minimums.items():
        print(f"  {'ok  ' if ok else 'MISS'} {rule}")
    if not all(minimums.values()):
        print("gen_fixture: a minimum was missed; nothing written", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    await _write_all(out, files)
    print(f"wrote {', '.join(sorted(files))} to {out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the scenario and save every dump and report the checker reads.

    python3 run_scenario.py --fixture fixture --small fixture_small --out run

Main scenario (run/main):
    load, apply, dump > before.jsonl, undo > report.json, dump > after.jsonl     timed for check 8
    undo again > report2.json, dump > after2.jsonl                              check 6
    copies of the database taken right after apply, each undone with CRASH_AFTER set (the first write,
    a few in the middle, the last, past the end, and two and three crashes in a row), a dump after each
    crash, then undo without it and a final dump                                check 7

Small fixture (run/small): ops_a, ops_b and ops_c, each undone in both orders from a fresh load.

The tool only ever runs as a subprocess, the way a person would run it. Runs that do not depend on each
other (the crashed copies, the small-fixture runs) go in parallel.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

from graph_undo.store import CRASH_EXIT_CODE

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
TOOL = [sys.executable, str(ROOT / "graphundo.py")]


class StepFailed(Exception):
    pass


async def tool(
    db: Path,
    *args: str | Path,
    stdout: Path | None = None,
    crash_after: int | None = None,
    expect: tuple[int, ...] = (0,),
) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """Run one graphundo command. Returns the exit code and stderr."""
    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "CRASH_AFTER"}
    if crash_after is not None:
        env["CRASH_AFTER"] = str(crash_after)
    proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
        *TOOL, "--db", str(db), *map(str, args),
        stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, env=env,
    )
    out, err = await proc.communicate()
    if stdout is not None:
        await asyncio.to_thread(stdout.write_bytes, out)
    message = err.decode()
    if proc.returncode not in expect:
        raise StepFailed(f"graphundo {' '.join(map(str, args))} exited {proc.returncode}: {message.strip()}")
    return proc.returncode or 0, message


def writes_of(stderr: str) -> int:
    """undo says on stderr how many writes it made."""
    match = re.search(r": (\d+) writes", stderr)
    if match is None:
        raise StepFailed(f"undo did not say how many writes it made: {stderr!r}")
    return int(match.group(1))


async def write_json(path: Path, value: object) -> None:
    await asyncio.to_thread(path.write_text, json.dumps(value, indent=2) + "\n", "utf-8")


# ---- main scenario ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


async def main_scenario(fixture: Path, out: Path, limit: asyncio.Semaphore) -> dict[str, object]:
    await asyncio.to_thread(out.mkdir, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    db = out / "graph.db"
    ops_text = await asyncio.to_thread((fixture / "ops.jsonl").read_text, "utf-8")
    delete_op = next(
        rec["op_id"] for rec in map(json.loads, filter(str.strip, ops_text.splitlines()))
        if rec.get("kind") == "delete_subtree"
    )

    steps: dict[str, float] = {}

    async def timed(name: str, *args: str | Path, stdout: Path | None = None) -> str:
        start = time.perf_counter()
        _, err = await tool(db, *args, stdout=stdout)
        steps[name] = round(time.perf_counter() - start, 3)
        return err

    await timed("load", "load", fixture / "seed.jsonl", stdout=out / "load.json")
    await timed("apply", "apply", fixture / "ops.jsonl", stdout=out / "apply.json")
    await asyncio.to_thread(shutil.copyfile, db, out / "after_apply.db")  # for the crashed runs; not timed
    await timed("dump_before", "dump", stdout=out / "before.jsonl")
    writes = writes_of(await timed("undo", "undo", delete_op, stdout=out / "report.json"))
    await timed("dump_after", "dump", stdout=out / "after.jsonl")
    scenario_seconds = round(sum(steps.values()), 3)
    print(f"main: load+apply+dump+undo+dump in {scenario_seconds:.2f}s, undo made {writes} writes")

    _, err = await tool(db, "undo", delete_op, stdout=out / "report2.json")
    second_writes = writes_of(err)
    await tool(db, "dump", stdout=out / "after2.jsonl")

    plans = {f"at_{n:05d}": [n] for n in sorted({1, 2, 3, writes // 4, writes // 2, 3 * writes // 4, writes - 1, writes})}
    plans[f"at_{writes + 1:05d}_past_end"] = [writes + 1]
    plans["twice"] = [writes // 3, writes // 3]
    plans["three_times"] = [writes // 5, writes // 5, writes // 5]

    async def crashed(name: str, points: list[int]) -> None:
        async with limit:
            d = out / "crash" / name
            await asyncio.to_thread(d.mkdir, parents=True)
            copy = d / "graph.db"
            await asyncio.to_thread(shutil.copyfile, out / "after_apply.db", copy)
            codes = []
            for i, n in enumerate(points):

    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "CRASH_AFTER"}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Break the undo on purpose, one way at a time, and show which checks catch each break.

    python3 mutation_check.py

Each mutation is a small edit to a copy of this repository in a temporary directory. For every copy the
script generates both fixtures, runs the scenario and runs the checker. A checker that passes a broken
undo would prove nothing, so every mutation below must make at least one check fail. Exit status 0 when
every mutation is caught. Takes about a minute.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import re
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

# name -> [(file, text to find, replacement)]
MUTATIONS: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str, str]]] = {
    "merge overwrites what a person wrote": [
        ("graph_undo/undo.py",
         "old_is_newer = old_w is not None and (live_w is None or old_w[0] > live_w[0])",
         "old_is_newer = old_w is not None"),
    ],
    "tags not recomputed after a step": [
        ("graph_undo/undo.py",
         "            # Recompute what this step can have changed: the node and everything now below it.\n"
         "            await refresh_subtree(store, target)\n",
         "            pass\n"),
    ],
    "arrows a person moved away come back": [
        ("graph_undo/undo.py",
         '"AND seq > (SELECT seq FROM ops WHERE op_id = ?) LIMIT 1"',
         '"AND seq > (SELECT seq FROM ops WHERE op_id = ?) AND 0 LIMIT 1"'),
    ],
    "no transaction per step": [
        ("graph_undo/store.py", '        await self._call(self._conn.execute, "BEGIN IMMEDIATE")\n', "        pass\n"),
        ("graph_undo/store.py", '            await self._call(self._conn.execute, "COMMIT")\n', "            pass\n"),
        ("graph_undo/store.py",
         '            await self._call(self._conn.execute, "ROLLBACK")\n            raise\n        try:',
         "            raise\n        try:"),
    ],
    "report leaves out one arrow": [
        ("graph_undo/undo.py",
         "    for from_id, to_id, edge_type, outcome, reason, waiting_on, now_from, now_to in edge_rows:",
         "    for from_id, to_id, edge_type, outcome, reason, waiting_on, now_from, now_to in edge_rows[:-1]:"),
    ],
    "restored even when the name is taken": [
        ("graph_undo/undo.py",
         'holder = await store.fetchval("SELECT id FROM nodes WHERE qualified_name = ?", (row.qualified_name,))',
         "holder = None"),
        ("graph_undo/schema.py", "qualified_name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,", "qualified_name TEXT NOT NULL,"),
    ],
    "waiting rows never retried": [
        ("graph_undo/undo.py", "        await self.retry_waiting()\n", "        pass\n"),
    ],
    "no 24-hour limit": [
        ("graph_undo/undo.py", "        if age > UNDO_WINDOW:\n", "        if False:\n"),
    ],
    "a started undo is held to the 24 hours too": [
        ("graph_undo/undo.py",
         "            return  # started before: it can always finish, whatever the clock says\n",
         "            if now - datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(applied_at) > UNDO_WINDOW:\n"
         "                raise UndoError(\"more than 24 hours\")\n"
         "            return\n"),
    ],
    "skipped rows decided again on every run": [
        ("graph_undo/undo.py",
         "    if retrying_for is None:\n        return outcome is None",
         "    if retrying_for is None:\n        return outcome in (None, SKIPPED)"),
        ("graph_undo/undo.py",
         '"SELECT id FROM removed_nodes WHERE delete_op = ? AND outcome IS NULL ORDER BY ord"',
         "\"SELECT id FROM removed_nodes WHERE delete_op = ? AND (outcome IS NULL OR outcome = 'skipped') ORDER BY ord\""),
    ],
}

STEPS = [
    ["gen_fixture.py", "--seed", "7", "--out", "fixture"],
    ["gen_fixture.py", "--small", "--out", "fixture_small"],
    ["run_scenario.py", "--fixture", "fixture", "--small", "fixture_small", "--out", "run"],
]
CHECK = ["checker.py", "--fixture", "fixture", "--small", "fixture_small", "--run", "run"]


async def run(cwd: Path, args: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str]:
    proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
        sys.executable, *args, cwd=cwd, stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT
    )
    out, _ = await proc.communicate()
    return proc.returncode or 0, out.decode()


def _prepare(target: Path, edits: list[tuple[str, str, str]]) -> None:
    shutil.copytree(
        ROOT, target,
        ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns(".git", "run", "fixture", "fixture_small", "__pycache__", "*.db", "*.db-*"),
    )
    for rel, old, new in edits:
        path = target / rel
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        if old not in text:
            raise SystemExit(f"mutation_check: {rel} no longer contains {old[:70]!r}; update MUTATIONS")
        path.write_text(text.replace(old, new, 1), encoding="utf-8")


async def mutate(name: str, edits: list[tuple[str, str, str]], work: Path, limit: asyncio.Semaphore) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    async with limit:
        target = work / re.sub(r"\W+", "_", name)
        await asyncio.to_thread(_prepare, target, edits)
        for step in STEPS:
            code, out = await run(target, step)
            if code != 0:
                return name, [f"({step[0]} failed: {out.strip().splitlines()[-1] if out.strip() else code})"]
        _, out = await run(target, CHECK)
        caught = sorted({re.split(r"\s{2,}", line)[1] for line in out.splitlines() if line.startswith("FAIL")})
        return name, caught


async def main() -> int:
    work = Path(await asyncio.to_thread(tempfile.mkdtemp, prefix="graphundo-mutants-"))
    try:
        limit = asyncio.Semaphore(3)
        results = await asyncio.gather(*(mutate(n, e, work, limit) for n, e in MUTATIONS.items()))
    finally:
        await asyncio.to_thread(shutil.rmtree, work, True)
    missed = 0
    for name, caught in results:
        print(f"{'CAUGHT' if caught else 'MISSED'}  {name}")
        for check in caught:
            print(f"          by: {check}")
        missed += not caught
    print(f"\n{len(results) - missed} of {len(results)} mutations caught")
    return 0 if missed == 0 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

# Undo in a shared graph

A command-line tool that keeps a graph of entities and relationships in one SQLite file, and can undo a
subtree delete after other people and an ingest job have kept editing the graph. Instead of rolling the
graph back, undo puts back what the delete removed on top of the graph as it is now. For every removed
node and arrow it reports one outcome: restored, merged or skipped. The rules it follows are in
[DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md).

Python 3.11 or newer. Nothing to install: everything comes from the standard library.

## Run it

```bash
python3 gen_fixture.py --seed 7 --out fixture
python3 gen_fixture.py --small --out fixture_small
python3 run_scenario.py --fixture fixture --small fixture_small --out run
python3 checker.py --fixture fixture --small fixture_small --run run
```

1. Writes `fixture/seed.jsonl` (1,717 nodes and 3,034 arrows), `fixture/ops.jsonl` (one delete of 620
   nodes, then 300 operations) and `fixture/planted.json`. Prints the counts the task asks for and stops
   with an error, writing nothing, if one is missed. Same seed, same files.
2. Writes the six-node fixture used for the rules that need two deletes: `seed.jsonl`, `ops_a.jsonl`,
   `ops_b.jsonl`, `ops_c.jsonl`.
3. Runs the tool as a subprocess and saves every dump and report under `run/`. The main scenario is
   load, apply, dump, undo, dump (timed). Then it runs undo a second time, and runs 11 crashed undos on
   copies of the database taken right after apply. Next come the 24-hour limit runs, with the clock set
   past the limit, exactly at it, and across it. Last, it runs the six-node fixture in both undo orders
   for each operations file. Takes about 7 seconds.
4. Reads only files and never runs the tool. Prints one PASS or FAIL line per check, and exits with
   status 0 when every check passes.

Optional: `python3 mutation_check.py` breaks the undo in 10 different ways, each in a throwaway copy of
the repository, and shows which checks catch each break. It takes about a minute and exits with status 0
when every break is caught.

## The scenario by hand

```bash
python3 graphundo.py load fixture/seed.jsonl
python3 graphundo.py apply fixture/ops.jsonl
python3 graphundo.py dump > before.jsonl
python3 graphundo.py undo op0001 > report.json
python3 graphundo.py dump > after.jsonl
```

The delete is the first operation, `op0001`. The database is `graph.db` in the current directory. Use
`--db PATH` or `GRAPHUNDO_DB` to put it somewhere else.

A crash and a resume, on a database where the delete has not been undone yet:

```bash
CRASH_AFTER=500 python3 graphundo.py undo op0001    # stops after 500 writes, exit status 3
python3 graphundo.py dump                           # a smaller graph, still whole, tags correct
python3 graphundo.py undo op0001                    # carries on: same final dump and report
```

## Commands

- `load SEED`: creates a new database from the seed, replacing an old one. The seed is checked first:
  ids are UUIDs, ids and names are unique, every arrow joins two seed nodes, no node has two parents and
  there is no loop. `effective_tags` is worked out for the whole graph.
- `apply OPS`: applies the operations in order, one transaction each. An operation that cannot be applied
  as written is stored as rejected, with its reason, and changes nothing. Running apply again skips op_ids
  that were already applied.
- `undo OP_ID`: undoes one `delete_subtree` and prints the report. Any other op_id prints an error and
  writes nothing. It reads `CRASH_AFTER=<n>`. On stderr it says how many writes it made. Undo is offered
  for 24 hours after the delete was applied (see below).
- `dump`: prints the live graph as JSONL. Node lines come first, sorted by id. Arrow lines follow, sorted
  by from_id, to_id and type. Equal graphs print the same bytes.

## Input files

```json
{"kind": "node", "id": "…uuid…", "qualified_name": "warehouse.sales.orders", "type": "table", "description": "Orders in sales", "owner": "asha", "tags": ["pii"]}
{"kind": "edge", "from_id": "…", "to_id": "…", "type": "contains"}
```

Each operation line has `op_id`, `actor` (`human` or `ingest`) and `kind`:

```json
{"op_id": "op0001", "actor": "human",  "kind": "delete_subtree", "root_id": "…"}
{"op_id": "op0002", "actor": "human",  "kind": "edit_node", "id": "…", "set": {"owner": "ben", "tags": ["pii"]}}
{"op_id": "op0003", "actor": "human",  "kind": "add_edge", "from_id": "…", "to_id": "…", "type": "references"}
{"op_id": "op0004", "actor": "human",  "kind": "repoint_edge", "from_id": "…", "to_id": "…", "type": "references", "new_to_id": "…"}
{"op_id": "op0005", "actor": "ingest", "kind": "ingest_node", "qualified_name": "warehouse.sales.orders", "type": "table", "parent": "warehouse.sales"}
```

- `repoint_edge` takes exactly one of `new_from_id` and `new_to_id`. Re-pointing a contains arrow's
  `from_id` moves a node under another parent.
- `ingest_node` updates the type of the live node that has the name. When no live node has the name, it
  creates one under `parent`, if that parent is live, and at the top level otherwise. The new node's id is
  `uuid5(2f0c9a52-8a4e-4c55-9d1b-1b0f6d1e7a3c, "<op_id>/<qualified_name>")`, so later operations in the
  same file can refer to it. Ingest never sets description, owner or tags.
- `edit_node`, `repoint_edge` and `delete_subtree` are for people. `ingest_node` is for ingest.
  `add_edge` is for either.

## The report

```json
{
  "op_id": "op0001",
  "summary": {"nodes": {"restored": 547, "merged": 73, "skipped": 0}, "edges": {"restored": 531, "merged": 497, "skipped": 4}},
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "…", "qualified_name": "warehouse.sales.employees", "outcome": "merged", "reason": "name_in_use", "merged_into": "…", "filled": ["description", "tags"], "kept_live": ["owner"], "not_restored": {"owner": "jo"}},
    {"id": "…", "qualified_name": "warehouse.sales.invoices", "outcome": "restored"}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"from": "…", "to": "…", "type": "references", "outcome": "skipped", "reason": "removed_by_person", "now": ["…", "…"]}
  ]
}
```

The report has one entry for every node and arrow the delete removed, in parents-first order. `merged`
and `skipped` entries always carry a reason. A merged node lists the fields filled from the journal,
the fields that kept their live value, and the old values that were not applied. A merged or skipped
arrow shows where its ends are now (`now`). A row blocked by a later delete names that delete in
`waiting_on`. Undoing that delete retries the row, and the next printout of this report shows the new
outcome.

## What the checker checks

The checker imports nothing from the tool. It replays the seed and the operations in plain dictionaries,
then compares the replay with the saved dumps and reports.

- **0** The dump before undo equals the replayed graph, so apply did what the operations say.
- **1** Nothing a person did after the delete is lost: the fields they wrote, the arrows they added,
  the arrows they moved away and the nodes they deleted are all as they were just before undo.
- **2** Every removed node whose name is free, and whose parent is live or merged, is back under its
  old id with its description, owner and tags.
- **3** No two live nodes share a qualified_name.
- **4** The report lists every removed node and arrow exactly once, and each outcome matches the dump.
  A restored row is live, a merged row's target is live under the same name, and a skipped row is absent.
- **5** `effective_tags` recomputed from the dump matches, and no arrow points at a missing node.
- **6** A second undo gives the same dump and the same report, byte for byte, and writes nothing.
- **7** Crashed undos (CRASH_AFTER = the first write, a few in the middle, the last, past the end, two
  and three crashes in a row) finish with the same dump and report as a clean run. A dump between runs
  has no arrow to a missing node, has correct tags and has unique names.
- **8** Load, apply, dump, undo and dump take under 60 seconds. They take about 1.5 seconds.
- **24-hour limit** One second past the limit, undo refuses, says why and leaves the graph unchanged.
  Exactly at the limit it works. A finished undo prints its report again two days later and writes
  nothing. An undo that crashed before the limit and resumes after it finishes with the clean result.

It also checks the 11 cases the generator planted (`planted.json`) and, for the six small runs: undoing
both deletes gives back the dump right after load, byte for byte (files a and b). Rows blocked by d2
wait on d2 and come back when d2 is undone. File c ends with one `sales.orders` owned by ben, of type
view, with the old description and tags, and the two undo orders differ only in which id survives.

## Repository

- `graphundo.py`: the command-line entry point.
- `graph_undo/store.py`: async access to SQLite. Every sqlite3 call runs on one worker thread behind
  an async API, so the event loop never blocks on the disk. It counts writes for CRASH_AFTER.
- `graph_undo/schema.py`: the live tables (`nodes`, `edges`) and the journal (`ops`, `field_writes`,
  `edge_removals`, `removed_nodes`, `removed_edges`).
- `graph_undo/loader.py`, `applier.py`, `tags.py`, `undo.py`, `dumper.py`, `cli.py`: load, apply, the
  tag propagator, undo, dump and the command line.
- `gen_fixture.py`, `run_scenario.py`, `checker.py`, `mutation_check.py`: test data, harness, checker,
  and the checker's own test.

## The 24-hour limit

Undo is offered for 24 hours after the delete was applied. `apply` stores the time each operation ran,
and `undo` checks the clock when it first starts. Past the limit it refuses, writes nothing and says
why, and the journal rows stay. An undo that has started can always finish: a crashed run resumes and
a finished run prints its report again, whatever the clock says.

The operations in the fixture carry no times, so the 24 hours start when `apply` runs. A database applied
more than a day ago refuses undo; run `load` and `apply` again to start over. For tests,
`GRAPHUNDO_NOW=2026-01-02T00:00:01+00:00` (an ISO 8601 time with a zone) replaces the clock that `apply`
and `undo` read.

The database is one SQLite file in SQLite's default rollback-journal mode. The only other file is the
journal SQLite keeps during a transaction. A crash can leave that journal next to the database, and
the next command that opens the database rolls the unfinished step back.

# Undo in a shared graph

A command-line tool that keeps a graph of entities and relationships in one SQLite file, and can undo a
subtree delete after other people and an ingest job have kept editing the graph. Instead of rolling the
graph back, undo puts back what the delete removed on top of the graph as it is now. For every removed
node and arrow it reports one outcome: restored, merged or skipped. The rules it follows are in
[DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md).

Python 3.11 or newer. Nothing to install: everything comes from the standard library.

## Run it

```bash
python3 gen_fixture.py --seed 7 --out fixture
python3 gen_fixture.py --small --out fixture_small
python3 run_scenario.py --fixture fixture --small fixture_small --out run
python3 checker.py --fixture fixture --small fixture_small --run run
```

1. Writes `fixture/seed.jsonl` (1,717 nodes and 3,034 arrows), `fixture/ops.jsonl` (one delete of 620
   nodes, then 300 operations) and `fixture/planted.json`. Prints the counts the task asks for and stops
   with an error, writing nothing, if one is missed. Same seed, same files.
2. Writes the six-node fixture used for the rules that need two deletes: `seed.jsonl`, `ops_a.jsonl`,
   `ops_b.jsonl`, `ops_c.jsonl`.
3. Runs the tool as a subprocess and saves every dump and report under `run/`. The main scenario is
   load, apply, dump, undo, dump (timed). Then it runs undo a second time, and runs 11 crashed undos on
   copies of the database taken right after apply. Last, it runs the six-node fixture in both undo
   orders for each operations file. Takes about 7 seconds.
4. Reads only files and never runs the tool. Prints one PASS or FAIL line per check, and exits with
   status 0 when every check passes.

Optional: `python3 mutation_check.py` breaks the undo in 8 different ways, each in a throwaway copy of
the repository, and shows which checks catch each break. It takes about a minute and exits with status 0
when every break is caught.

## The scenario by hand

```bash
python3 graphundo.py load fixture/seed.jsonl
python3 graphundo.py apply fixture/ops.jsonl
python3 graphundo.py dump > before.jsonl
python3 graphundo.py undo op0001 > report.json
python3 graphundo.py dump > after.jsonl
```

The delete is the first operation, `op0001`. The database is `graph.db` in the current directory. Use
`--db PATH` or `GRAPHUNDO_DB` to put it somewhere else.

A crash and a resume, on a database where the delete has not been undone yet:

```bash
CRASH_AFTER=500 python3 graphundo.py undo op0001    # stops after 500 writes, exit status 3
python3 graphundo.py dump                           # a smaller graph, still whole, tags correct
python3 graphundo.py undo op0001                    # carries on: same final dump and report
```

## Commands

- `load SEED`: creates a new database from the seed, replacing an old one. The seed is checked first:
  ids are UUIDs, ids and names are unique, every arrow joins two seed nodes, no node has two parents and
  there is no loop. `effective_tags` is worked out for the whole graph.
- `apply OPS`: applies the operations in order, one transaction each. An operation that cannot be applied
  as written is stored as rejected, with its reason, and changes nothing. Running apply again skips op_ids
  that were already applied.
- `undo OP_ID`: undoes one `delete_subtree` and prints the report. Any other op_id prints an error and
  writes nothing. It reads `CRASH_AFTER=<n>`. On stderr it says how many writes it made.
- `dump`: prints the live graph as JSONL. Node lines come first, sorted by id. Arrow lines follow, sorted
  by from_id, to_id and type. Equal graphs print the same bytes.

## Input files

```json
{"kind": "node", "id": "…uuid…", "qualified_name": "warehouse.sales.orders", "type": "table", "description": "Orders in sales", "owner": "asha", "tags": ["pii"]}
{"kind": "edge", "from_id": "…", "to_id": "…", "type": "contains"}
```

Each operation line has `op_id`, `actor` (`human` or `ingest`) and `kind`:

```json
{"op_id": "op0001", "actor": "human",  "kind": "delete_subtree", "root_id": "…"}
{"op_id": "op0002", "actor": "human",  "kind": "edit_node", "id": "…", "set": {"owner": "ben", "tags": ["pii"]}}
{"op_id": "op0003", "actor": "human",  "kind": "add_edge", "from_id": "…", "to_id": "…", "type": "references"}
{"op_id": "op0004", "actor": "human",  "kind": "repoint_edge", "from_id": "…", "to_id": "…", "type": "references", "new_to_id": "…"}
{"op_id": "op0005", "actor": "ingest", "kind": "ingest_node", "qualified_name": "warehouse.sales.orders", "type": "table", "parent": "warehouse.sales"}
```

- `repoint_edge` takes exactly one of `new_from_id` and `new_to_id`. Re-pointing a contains arrow's
  `from_id` moves a node under another parent.
- `ingest_node` updates the type of the live node that has the name. When no live node has the name, it
  creates one under `parent`, if that parent is live, and at the top level otherwise. The new node's id is
  `uuid5(2f0c9a52-8a4e-4c55-9d1b-1b0f6d1e7a3c, "<op_id>/<qualified_name>")`, so later operations in the
  same file can refer to it. Ingest never sets description, owner or tags.
- `edit_node`, `repoint_edge` and `delete_subtree` are for people. `ingest_node` is for ingest.
  `add_edge` is for either.

## The report

```json
{
  "op_id": "op0001",
  "summary": {"nodes": {"restored": 547, "merged": 73, "skipped": 0}, "edges": {"restored": 531, "merged": 497, "skipped": 4}},
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "…", "qualified_name": "warehouse.sales.employees", "outcome": "merged", "reason": "name_in_use", "merged_into": "…", "filled": ["description", "tags"], "kept_live": ["owner"], "not_restored": {"owner": "jo"}},
    {"id": "…", "qualified_name": "warehouse.sales.invoices", "outcome": "restored"}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {"from": "…", "to": "…", "type": "references", "outcome": "skipped", "reason": "removed_by_person", "now": ["…", "…"]}
  ]
}
```

The report has one entry for every node and arrow the delete removed, in parents-first order. `merged`
and `skipped` entries always carry a reason. A merged node lists the fields filled from the journal,
the fields that kept their live value, and the old values that were not applied. A merged or skipped
arrow shows where its ends are now (`now`). A row blocked by a later delete names that delete in
`waiting_on`. Undoing that delete retries the row, and the next printout of this report shows the new
outcome.

## What the checker checks

The checker imports nothing from the tool. It replays the seed and the operations in plain dictionaries,
then compares the replay with the saved dumps and reports.

- **0** The dump before undo equals the replayed graph, so apply did what the operations say.
- **1** Nothing a person did after the delete is lost: the fields they wrote, the arrows they added,
  the arrows they moved away and the nodes they deleted are all as they were just before undo.
- **2** Every removed node whose name is free, and whose parent is live or merged, is back under its
  old id with its description, owner and tags.
- **3** No two live nodes share a qualified_name.
- **4** The report lists every removed node and arrow exactly once, and each outcome matches the dump.
  A restored row is live, a merged row's target is live under the same name, and a skipped row is absent.
- **5** `effective_tags` recomputed from the dump matches, and no arrow points at a missing node.
- **6** A second undo gives the same dump and the same report, byte for byte, and writes nothing.
- **7** Crashed undos (CRASH_AFTER = the first write, a few in the middle, the last, past the end, two
  and three crashes in a row) finish with the same dump and report as a clean run. A dump between runs
  has no arrow to a missing node, has correct tags and has unique names.
- **8** Load, apply, dump, undo and dump take under 60 seconds. They take about 1.5 seconds.

It also checks the 11 cases the generator planted (`planted.json`) and, for the six small runs: undoing
both deletes gives back the dump right after load, byte for byte (files a and b). Rows blocked by d2
wait on d2 and come back when d2 is undone. File c ends with one `sales.orders` owned by ben, of type
view, with the old description and tags, and the two undo orders differ only in which id survives.

## Repository

- `graphundo.py`: the command-line entry point.
- `graph_undo/store.py`: async access to SQLite. Every sqlite3 call runs on one worker thread behind
  an async API, so the event loop never blocks on the disk. It counts writes for CRASH_AFTER.
- `graph_undo/schema.py`: the live tables (`nodes`, `edges`) and the journal (`ops`, `field_writes`,
  `edge_removals`, `removed_nodes`, `removed_edges`).
- `graph_undo/loader.py`, `applier.py`, `tags.py`, `undo.py`, `dumper.py`, `cli.py`: load, apply, the
  tag propagator, undo, dump and the command line.
- `gen_fixture.py`, `run_scenario.py`, `checker.py`, `mutation_check.py`: test data, harness, checker,
  and the checker's own test.

## The 24-hour limit

Undo is offered for 24 hours after the delete was applied. `apply` stores the time each operation ran,
and `undo` checks the clock when it first starts. Past the limit it refuses, writes nothing and says
why, and the journal rows stay. An undo that has started can always finish: a crashed run resumes and
a finished run prints its report again, whatever the clock says.

The operations in the fixture carry no times, so the 24 hours start when `apply` runs. A database applied
more than a day ago refuses undo; run `load` and `apply` again to start over. For tests,
`GRAPHUNDO_NOW=2026-01-02T00:00:01+00:00` (an ISO 8601 time with a zone) replaces the clock that `apply`
and `undo` read.

The database is one SQLite file in SQLite's default rollback-journal mode. The only other file is the
journal SQLite keeps during a transaction. A crash can leave that journal next to the database, and
the next command that opens the database rolls the unfinished step back.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Decisions

Undo does not roll the graph back. It applies the inverse of one delete to the graph as it is now: it
only adds rows and fills fields, and never removes a row or replaces a value a person wrote after the
delete.

## Conflict rules

**Independent edits** touched something the delete did not, such as the deleted root's parent or
siblings, a dashboard that pointed into the deleted area, or a node created elsewhere. Rule: undo leaves
them exactly as they are, and restored nodes pick up their effects. A tag a person added above the
deleted root flows into every restored node below it.

**Conflicting edits** wrote a field that undo would also write. Rule: for each field, the most recent
write wins.
- The seed counts as written at the start.
- A value put back by an undo keeps the time of its original write.
- Everything in the journal was written before the delete, so a value a person wrote after the delete
  always wins. The journal value is then listed under `not_restored`.
- A field nobody wrote is filled from the journal.
- A field a person emptied on purpose stays empty. `field_writes` tells it apart from a field nobody wrote.
- Tags count as one value: the two lists are never mixed.
- `effective_tags` is never copied back. Undo recomputes it from the live graph in every step.
- `type` follows the same rule, with ingest as the writer.

**Caused edits** only happened because the delete did. The typical case: the ingest found a name free
and created a new node with a new id. Rule: undo treats it as the same thing coming back. It merges the
old node into the live one, keeps the live id (everything made since already points at it), and re-aims
the old arrows at it.

## The decisions undo makes

For each removed node, parents first, one transaction per node:
- Its name is held by a live node: **merged** into that node.
- Otherwise its parent is live, or was merged: **restored** with its old id and all its fields.
- Otherwise: **skipped** (`parent_not_live`). `waiting_on` names the delete that holds the parent.

For each removed arrow, after resolving each end to where it is now. The first match wins:
1. An end is not live: skipped (`endpoint_not_live`), waiting on that end's delete.
2. The arrow already exists: merged (`already_present`).
3. It is a contains arrow and the child already has a parent: skipped (`child_has_other_parent`).
   The later placement wins.
4. A person re-pointed this arrow away after the delete: skipped (`removed_by_person`).
5. It would make a node its own ancestor: skipped (`would_create_cycle`).
6. Otherwise it is added: restored, or merged (`endpoint_merged`) when an end was merged.

Undoing a later delete retries the rows that were waiting on it: newest journal first, then parents
first. In this order nothing has to wait. A row that already has an outcome is never decided again.
That makes a second run write nothing, and a crashed run resume from its last committed step.

Undo is offered for 24 hours after the delete. After about a day of edits by others there are as many
edits as deleted nodes, and the report is too long to review. The clock is checked only when an undo
first starts, so a crashed or finished undo can always run again.

No code breaks a hard requirement in the PDF. What goes against the PDF is three deliverables that aren't done yet. Against your design, there are a handful of real deviations and two judgment calls a grader could read differently. I audited the code against both documents, had a second, independent reviewer do the same, and checked every finding in the code myself.

**Against the PDF: deliverables still missing**
1. DECISIONS.md has two required sections still as placeholders (`DECISIONS.md:53` and `:57`): what the model proposed that you rejected, and what you verified yourself. The PDF grades exactly these, and only you can write them.
2. No AI sessions are in the repo or linked from it. This session counts and has to be shared unedited.
3. The repo has no commits; every file is untracked.

**Could be read as against the PDF (your call)**

4. **Seed size.** We read "about 5,000 nodes and edges" as about 5,000 lines in total: 1,717 nodes and 3,034 arrows. Your design reads it the same way ("about 5,000 rows"). A grader who reads it as about 5,000 nodes sees a third of that, and the 620-node delete removes 36% of the graph. Scaling the generator up is cheap and stays well under 60 seconds.

5. **Actor rules.** Operations from the wrong kind of actor are rejected (`applier.py:141, 170, 197, 227`): ingest can't edit, re-point or delete, and people can't ingest.
   - The PDF only requires that ingest never sets description, owner or tags, and it puts authorisation out of scope.
   - Your design lists "checking who is allowed to do what" as not part of the tool, yet assigns each operation to an actor.
   - A grader's own ops file containing, say, a delete by ingest would be rejected.

6. **`CRASH_AFTER`.** The tool stops right after the n-th write, before that step is saved, so `CRASH_AFTER=1` leaves the graph unchanged. That's what your design says. Someone reading "exits after n writes" literally might expect n writes to be kept. Low risk.

7. **Which operations undo accepts.** The PDF says "undo <op_id>. Apply the inverse of that operation". Your design limits undo to subtree deletes and errors on anything else. The rest of the PDF supports that ("any delete-subtree can be undone later"), so the risk is low.

**Code that goes against the design**

8. **Checker command.** The design runs `python checker.py fixture before.jsonl after.jsonl report.json`. Ours takes `--fixture --small --run` and needs the run script's whole output folder (`checker.py:565-567`). That means the files from the README's by-hand steps can't be checked.

9. **Re-used op_id.** `apply` silently skips an op_id that's already in the database, even when the line is a different operation (`applier.py:98`). I tested it: a second file that used `d1` for an edit was skipped and the edit never happened. The design doesn't call for this skip at all.

10. **Check 8.** It times only the load-to-dump steps, about 1.5 s. The design's run-script paragraph says to time the whole run; that time, about 7 s, is recorded but never checked (`checker.py:375`). There's no practical risk.

11. **Third fixture file.** The design says the generator writes "the same two files" and that the checker works out expected results on its own. The generator also writes `planted.json`, and the planted-case checks read their node ids from it. The eight invariants don't depend on it.

12. **README claim.** The README says the SQLite journal is the only other file. But `load` also builds `graph.db.loading` and then renames it (`loader.py:32`).

13. **Who runs the extra undos.** The design's list of checks says the checker runs undo a second time and copies the database for the crash runs. Its scenario paragraph says the run script does that. We followed the scenario paragraph.

**Where the design is unclear and the code picked one side**

14. **Merge rule.** The design says both "filled only if no person has written that field" and "most recent write wins". The code uses most recent write wins, which story 4 needs. One side effect: when the journal value wins, the report doesn't show the live value it replaced. In ops_c, undoing d1 then d2 changes owner asha to ben and type table to view, but the report only says `filled: ["owner","type"]`.

15. **Type tracking and extra columns.** The design's tables keep write times for three fields, but its type rule needs a fourth, so the code tracks type too. The code also adds the columns that behaviour needs: `ops.kind/reason/payload`, `removed_nodes.detail` and `removed_edges.ord`.

16. **Small fixture coverage.** The design says "each story is also the description of a test", but the small fixture covers only stories 2–4. Stories 1, 5 and 6 are covered by planted cases in the main fixture. The reviewer also ran them by hand, and the results match the design.

17. **Undo isn't recorded.** The design lists undo among the changes that record who made them, but undo isn't recorded as an operation. That only matters if you add redo.

**Additions the design doesn't mention.** None of these conflict with it:
- the report's `summary` block, and `now` shown on skipped arrows
- an 11th planted case, plus 3 planted operations that are meant to be rejected, so 297 of the 300 apply
- extra checks: check 0, the planted cases, and three crashes in a row
- retries take the newest delete first, which chained deletes need
- the async store, the `--db` option, and the write count printed on stderr

I'd fix 8, 9, 10 and 12 now: they're small, clear-cut, and either bring the code in line with your design or fix a real surprise. 4, 5 and 14 are design decisions for you. Should I fix those four now, or leave everything as it is?

"""Reads and writes on the live graph that apply, undo and the tag propagator share."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict, deque
from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator, Mapping, Sequence
from typing import NamedTuple

from .store import Store

# A node and everything below it along contains arrows, each with its contains parent. UNION (not
# UNION ALL) drops a node it has already found, so the walk ends even if a contains loop ever existed.
SUBTREE_SQL = """
WITH RECURSIVE sub(id) AS (
    SELECT ?
    UNION
    SELECT e.to_id FROM edges e JOIN sub ON e.from_id = sub.id WHERE e.type = 'contains'
)
SELECT n.id, n.qualified_name, n.type, n.description, n.owner, n.tags, n.effective_tags,
       (SELECT p.from_id FROM edges p WHERE p.to_id = n.id AND p.type = 'contains')
FROM sub JOIN nodes n ON n.id = sub.id
"""

# Walk up from the second id along contains arrows; 1 when the first id is on the way (or is the second).
ANCESTOR_OR_SELF_SQL = """
WITH RECURSIVE up(id) AS (
    SELECT ?2
    UNION
    SELECT e.from_id FROM edges e JOIN up ON e.to_id = up.id WHERE e.type = 'contains'
)
SELECT 1 FROM up WHERE id = ?1 LIMIT 1
"""


class SubtreeRow(NamedTuple):
    id: str
    qualified_name: str
    type: str
    description: str | None
    owner: str | None
    tags: str
    effective_tags: str
    parent_id: str | None


def walk_down(roots: Iterable[str], children: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]]) -> Iterator[tuple[str, str | None]]:
    """Every node below the roots once, parents before children, as (node, parent). Siblings in id order."""
    queue: deque[tuple[str, str | None]] = deque((root, None) for root in roots)
    seen: set[str] = set()
    while queue:
        node, parent = queue.popleft()
        if node in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(node)
        yield node, parent
        queue.extend((child, node) for child in sorted(children.get(node, ())))


async def subtree(store: Store, root: str) -> tuple[list[SubtreeRow], dict[str, list[str]]]:
    """The rows of root and everything below it, and the children of each of them."""
    rows = [SubtreeRow(*row) for row in await store.fetchall(SUBTREE_SQL, (root,))]
    children: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    for row in rows:
        if row.id != root and row.parent_id is not None:
            children[row.parent_id].append(row.id)
    return rows, children


async def node_live(store: Store, node_id: str) -> bool:
    return bool(await store.fetchval("SELECT 1 FROM nodes WHERE id = ?", (node_id,)))


async def edge_live(store: Store, from_id: str, to_id: str, edge_type: str) -> bool:
    return bool(
        await store.fetchval(
            "SELECT 1 FROM edges WHERE from_id = ? AND to_id = ? AND type = ?", (from_id, to_id, edge_type)
        )
    )


async def has_parent(store: Store, node_id: str) -> bool:
    return bool(await store.fetchval("SELECT 1 FROM edges WHERE to_id = ? AND type = 'contains'", (node_id,)))


async def ancestor_or_self(store: Store, ancestor: str, node_id: str) -> bool:
    """True when ancestor is node_id itself or above it along contains arrows."""
    return bool(await store.fetchval(ANCESTOR_OR_SELF_SQL, (ancestor, node_id)))


async def insert_edge(store: Store, from_id: str, to_id: str, edge_type: str) -> None:
    await store.write("INSERT INTO edges (from_id, to_id, type) VALUES (?, ?, ?)", (from_id, to_id, edge_type))


async def record_write(store: Store, node_id: str, field: str, seq: int, actor: str) -> None:
    """Remember who wrote this field of this node last, and in which operation."""
    await store.write(
        "INSERT INTO field_writes (node_id, field, seq, actor) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) "
        "ON CONFLICT (node_id, field) DO UPDATE SET seq = excluded.seq, actor = excluded.actor",
        (node_id, field, seq, actor),
    )

class SubtreeRow(NamedTuple):
    id: str
    qualified_name: str
    type: str
    description: str | None
    owner: str | None
    tags: str
    effective_tags: str
    parent_id: str | None


def walk_down(roots: Iterable[str], children: Mapping[str, Sequence[str]]) -> Iterator[tuple[str, str | None]]:
    """Every node below the roots once, parents before children, as (node, parent). Siblings in id order."""
    queue: deque[tuple[str, str | None]] = deque((root, None) for root in roots)
    seen: set[str] = set()
    while queue:
        node, parent = queue.popleft()
        if node in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(node)
        yield node, parent
        queue.extend((child, node) for child in sorted(children.get(node, ())))


async def subtree(store: Store, root: str) -> tuple[list[SubtreeRow], dict[str, list[str]]]:
    """The rows of root and everything below it, and the children of each of them."""
    rows = [SubtreeRow(*row) for row in await store.fetchall(SUBTREE_SQL, (root,))]
    children: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    for row in rows:
        if row.id != root and row.parent_id is not None:
            children[row.parent_id].append(row.id)
    return rows, children

    qualified_name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,   -- the table holds live nodes only: a name is unique among live nodes
    type           TEXT NOT NULL,
    description    TEXT,
    owner          TEXT,
    tags           TEXT NOT NULL,          -- JSON list, set by people, in the order written
    effective_tags TEXT NOT NULL           -- JSON list, worked out, sorted
);

CREATE TABLE edges (
    from_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES nodes(id),
    to_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES nodes(id),
    type    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('contains', 'references')),
    PRIMARY KEY (from_id, to_id, type)
);
-- A node has at most one contains parent: the contains arrows form a tree.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX one_parent ON edges(to_id) WHERE type = 'contains';
CREATE INDEX edges_by_to ON edges(to_id, type);

-- Every operation, applied or rejected. seq is the running number: "after the delete" means a larger seq.
-- Each undo is logged here too, once, as op_id 'undo:<op_id of the delete>' with kind 'undo', by a person,
-- so a later operation (or a redo) can tell what came after it.
CREATE TABLE ops (
    seq        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    op_id      TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    kind       TEXT NOT NULL,
    actor      TEXT NOT NULL,
    applied_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    status     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('applied', 'rejected')),
    reason     TEXT,
    payload    TEXT NOT NULL
);

-- Who wrote each field of each node last, and in which operation (seq 0 = the seed).
-- Tells "empty because nobody wrote it" from "a person cleared it on purpose".
-- Rows outlive their node, so a node restored with its old id keeps its write history.
CREATE TABLE field_writes (
    node_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    field   TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (field IN ('description', 'owner', 'tags', 'type')),
    seq     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    actor   TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (node_id, field)
);

-- Every arrow a person re-pointed away from its old end, with the operation's seq.
CREATE TABLE edge_removals (
    from_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    to_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
    type    TEXT NOT NULL,
    seq     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    actor   TEXT NOT NULL,
    op_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (from_id, to_id, type, seq)
);

-- A copy of each node a delete removed, and what undo decided for it.
CREATE TABLE removed_nodes (
    delete_op      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES ops(op_id),
    ord            INTEGER NOT NULL,       -- parents first
    id             TEXT NOT NULL,
    qualified_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    type           TEXT NOT NULL,
    description    TEXT,
    owner          TEXT,
    tags           TEXT NOT NULL,
    parent_id      TEXT,                   -- the contains parent at the time of the delete
    writes         TEXT NOT NULL,          -- JSON {field: [seq, actor]}, copied from field_writes
    outcome        TEXT CHECK (outcome IN ('restored', 'merged', 'skipped')),
    reason         TEXT,
    merged_into    TEXT,
    waiting_on     TEXT,                   -- the delete that has to be undone before this row can come back
    detail         TEXT,                   -- JSON for merged rows: filled, kept_live, not_restored, replaced
    decided_by     TEXT,                   -- the undo that wrote the outcome ('undo:<op_id>'; a retry names a later one)
    prior          TEXT,                   -- JSON for merged rows: {field: {value, write}} the live node held before
                                           -- undo changed it, so a redo can put it back
    PRIMARY KEY (delete_op, id)
);
CREATE INDEX removed_nodes_by_id ON removed_nodes(id);
CREATE INDEX removed_nodes_waiting ON removed_nodes(waiting_on) WHERE outcome = 'skipped';

-- A copy of each arrow a delete removed, and what undo decided for it.
CREATE TABLE removed_edges (
    delete_op  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES ops(op_id),
    ord        INTEGER NOT NULL,           -- arrows from parents in the order of their child, then the rest
    from_id    TEXT NOT NULL,
    to_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
    type       TEXT NOT NULL,
    outcome    TEXT CHECK (outcome IN ('restored', 'merged', 'skipped')),
    reason     TEXT,
    waiting_on TEXT,
    now_from   TEXT,                       -- where the arrow points now, once its ends were worked out
    now_to     TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (delete_op, from_id, to_id, type)
);
CREATE INDEX removed_edges_waiting ON removed_edges(waiting_on) WHERE outcome = 'skipped';
